description.value: The Engine 374 Pavilion houses the restored CPR locomotive that pulled Canada's first transcontinental passenger train into Vancouver on May 23, 1887. Housed in a glass pavilion at the corner of Davie Street and Pacific Boulevard, it is staffed by enthusiastic West Coast Railway Association volunteers who offer free tours of the engine and share its colourful history. It sits next to the Roundhouse Community Centre in Yaletown, a 10-minute walk from downtown Vancouver.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Engine 374 Pavilion is a free-admission museum housing the historic CPR Engine 374 that pulled the first transcontinental passenger train into Vancouver in 1887. It is staffed by volunteers from the West Coast Railway Association and located adjacent to the Roundhouse Community Centre. The website provides a phone number (604-713-1800 ext. 1) not present in OSM. No evidence was found on the website for bike parking, water refill, washrooms, or any of the optional amenities at the pavilion itself.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A free, historically significant railway museum in central Vancouver that would be a worthwhile stop for touring cyclists passing through the city. Easily accessible and well-maintained.

wow_evidence: The locomotive that pulled Canada's first transcontinental passenger train into Vancouver (1887); free glass pavilion, volunteer-staffed tours. National railway story.
